extinctions.name: End-Ordovician
extinctions.summary: A brief, severe ice age at the end of the Hirnantian. Most marine animals were on shallow shelves; the sea fell, then flooded back, and about 85 percent of species died. Graptolites, many brachiopods, and reef-building animals were hit hardest.

extinctions.name: Late Devonian
extinctions.summary: The Kellwasser crisis at the Frasnian–Famennian boundary, with a second blow at the end of the Devonian (the Hangenberg event, 358.86 Ma). Reefs collapsed, jawless fishes and many placoderms disappeared, and the great Devonian reef ecosystems never recovered.

extinctions.name: End-Permian
extinctions.summary: The largest extinction in the fossil record. Siberian Traps volcanism loaded the air with carbon dioxide, warmed the climate, acidified and deoxygenated the oceans, and killed roughly 80 to 90 percent of marine species and most land vertebrates. It closes the Paleozoic.

extinctions.name: End-Triassic
extinctions.summary: Central Atlantic Magmatic Province eruptions as the Atlantic began to open. Conodonts died out, many marine reptiles and amphibians vanished, and the large crocodile-line archosaurs that had dominated land lost out to the dinosaurs.

extinctions.name: End-Cretaceous
extinctions.summary: The Chicxulub impact, with Deccan Traps volcanism already stressing the climate. Non-bird dinosaurs, pterosaurs, ammonites, and marine reptiles disappeared. Birds, mammals, crocodilians, and many flowering plants made it through into the Paleocene.
